Article 8
(1) The community may participate and be responsible in the service, prevention, assistance, recovery and monitoring of victims of violence.
(2) Community participation and responsibility as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be implemented in the form of:
a. preventing the occurrence of acts of violence against Women and Children; b. providing information and/or reporting acts of violence against Women and Children to the competent authorities;
c. providing emergency assistance; and
d. providing protection to victims of violence.

REGARDING
PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE
I. GENERAL
Children are the future of the nation and the next generation of the nation's aspirations, so that every child has the right to survival, to grow and develop, to participate and has the right to protection from acts of violence and discrimination as well as civil rights and freedoms.
Likewise women who play a role as mothers who give birth to children who are healthy, strong, resilient, of noble character, potential and quality. Through the role of women and families, society and the state will produce resilient generations who will continue the nation's aspirations.
Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights so that their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and destiny without discrimination.
In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Katingan Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades their degree and human dignity, protection needs to be provided for Women and Children victims of violence so that it needs to be regulated in Regional Regulations.
So far, laws and regulations governing the protection of women and children victims of violence have not regulated protection efforts in the regions so that institutional support and regulations are needed that can guarantee their implementation.
This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, particularly in terms of prevention, implementation, handling, empowerment, guidance and supervision of the protection of women in Katingan Regency.

CHAPTER X
COMMUNITY PARTICIPATION
Article 15
(1) In providing protection to Women and Children victims of violence, the community may:
a. form family partners at the kelurahan and village level coordinating with Damang or Mantir Adat and Community Leaders;
b. form Women and Children protection units within community organizations;
c. conduct socialization of Women's and Children's rights independently; d. provide first aid to victims; and
e. report to the authorized agency if violence against victims occurs in their environment.
(2) Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out by individuals, family partners, social community institutions, non-governmental organizations, educational institutions, religious institutions, private sector, and mass media.

Article 3
Protection of Women and Children victims of violence aims to:
a. prevent all forms of violence against women and children; b. protect women and children as well as provide services to women and Children victims of violence; and
c. empower women and Children victims of violence.

CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is Katingan Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Government of Katingan Regency.
3. Regent is the Regent of Katingan.
4. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter referred to as DPRD is the Regional House of Representatives of Katingan Regency.
5. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to victims carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination.
6. Woman is an adult human being of female gender and a person who is legally recognized as a woman.
7. Child is a person who has not reached 18 years of age, including a Child in the womb.
8. Violence is any act that results in or causes misery and suffering whether physical, sexual, psychological including neglect, threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public and or in private life.
9. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens the integrity and degrades the dignity of the child.
- 4 -
10. Violence against women is any action or may result in misery or suffering to women physically, mentally sexually or psychologically including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or private life.
11. Victims of violence against women and children are individuals or groups, who experience misery and or suffering as a result of violence and or threats of violence.
12. Protection of women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the police, prosecutors, courts, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that violence against women will or has occurred.
13. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
14. Service is action taken as soon as possible to victims when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against women and children will, is or has occurred.
15. Companion is a person or representative from an institution/organization/agency providing services to victims of violence against women and children who is trained or has expertise in accordance with their competence and authority in providing assistance to victims of violence in accordance with the type of service provided.
16. Social rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly.
17. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims.
18. Legal Aid is legal services provided by companions and/or legal apparatus which includes providing legal consultation, exercising power of attorney, representing, accompanying, defending and taking other legal actions for victims of violence in accordance with their competence and authority.
19. Regional Technical Implementation Unit for the Protection of Women and Children hereinafter abbreviated as UPTD PPA is a functional technical implementation unit as the organizer of integrated services for women and children who experience violence discrimination and other problems.
20. Standard Operating Procedures hereinafter abbreviated as SOP are standard steps that must be taken in protecting victims starting from handling complaints, health rehabilitation, social rehabilitation, legal aid, recovery/psychological services, mediation up to repatriation and social reintegration.
21. Minimum Service Standards abbreviated as SPM are performance benchmarks for UPTD PPA services in providing services for handling complaints, health rehabilitation, social rehabilitation, legal aid, recovery/psychological services, mediation up to repatriation and social reintegration.
22. Social Protection House is a temporary residence, provided to give protection to victims in accordance with predetermined standards.

CHAPTER VII
SOCIAL PROTECTION HOUSE
Article 12
(1) The Regional Government is obligated to establish a Social Protection House and/or Safe House.
(2) The Social Protection House and/or Safe House as referred to in paragraph (1) is to guarantee the implementation of services by UPTD PPA. . 1 - 8 -
(3) For the implementation of services as referred to in paragraph (2), the Regional Government may utilize social protection houses and/or Safe Houses owned by the community or other social service institutions.

2.1.rationale: In the Indonesian text, Pasal 7(3) only assigns implementation to relevant Perangkat Daerah according to their duties/functions, and Pasal 9 describes UPTD PPA as a unit providing “pelayanan terpadu” and that it can “mewadahi” various service units (rumah aman, rumah singgah, etc.). However, this does not clearly establish a formal coordination mechanism/network (e.g., mandated inter-agency coordination forum, SOP for coordination across institutions, referral/coordination procedures, designated coordinating body across sectors). The judge over-interpreted “can accommodate” and general assignment of responsibility as a coordination mechanism. The English passages accurately reflect the Indonesian, so the error is mainly the judge’s lenient reasoning.

(2) Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out by individuals, family partners, social community institutions, non-governmental organizations, educational institutions, religious institutions, private sector, and mass media.

4.2.rationale: The Indonesian text includes ‘keadilan dan kesetaraan gender’ as a principle (Pasal 2 huruf b) and defines ‘kesetaraan gender’ in the explanation, but it does not mandate or describe an education program/curriculum on gender equality. Pasal 15(1)(c) only mentions ‘sosialisasi hak Perempuan dan Anak’ (socialization of women’s and children’s rights), which is not the same as gender equality education (e.g., structured gender equality training/education, school-based curriculum, public education specifically on gender equality norms). The judge inferred gender equality education from general rights socialization and the presence of a gender equality principle, which is a reasoning error rather than a translation or retrieval problem.
